text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000010 bills 99215 well above its risk-adjusted expectation at every complexity level, including low-complexity patients, but only two 99215 claims have documentation, too few to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern leans toward the concern. The elevated 99215 share holds within every complexity band, not only among sicker patients, and the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims carry simple diagnoses such as rash (R21), abdominal pain (R10.9) or follow-up (Z09) (e.g., C0003475, C0005250, C0005537). Against that, the provider's 99214 volume is also heavy, and the two documented 99215 claims (C0003750, C0003867) were supported at high MDM with about 48 to 49 minutes, so the documentation we have does not show inflation. With records for only about 1% of claims, and both 99214 mismatches (C0003446, C0005118) documented at low MDM with no time recorded, the documentation is too thin to judge, and the note signals (missing audit trail, a few repeated-time and no-lab data claims) are weak and nonspecific. A reviewer should first request charts targeted at the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet, plus a larger 99214 sample, to see whether the documented MDM supports the billed level where patient complexity does not."}
